settings.vibe: fluorescent-lit, patient, no music telling you what to feel

concept.summary: Two estranged brothers have one weekend to inventory their dead father's hardware store before the buyer takes possession Monday morning. Frank, who stayed and ran the register for twenty years, wants to sell every last hinge at its marked price. Charlie, who left at eighteen and came back for the funeral, keeps finding things that aren't for sale — a repair ledger full of forgiven debts, a shoebox of returned keys, their mother's handwriting on a layaway card from 1989. The count has to balance by Monday. Neither brother's version of their father does.

characters.name: Frank Okafor
characters.backstory: Ran the store beside his father for twenty years; knows every SKU and none of his father's friends.
characters.motivations: Close the sale clean and prove staying was worth something.
characters.want: The inventory balanced and the check cashed by Monday.
characters.need: To learn what his father actually spent the store on.
characters.arc: From balancing the count to honoring what was never counted.

characters.name: Charlie Okafor
characters.backstory: Left at eighteen after a fight nobody names; came back for the funeral with a rental car and no black suit.
characters.motivations: Find proof the old man was more than the register.
characters.want: One object from the store that means something.
characters.need: To admit staying was also a choice someone made for him.
characters.voice: charming, evasive, lands one true sentence per day
